verdict: Agentic extraction is a good place to start for long lists. On synthetic statements with Claude Haiku 5.5, single-pass returned every row at 100 rows, but from 400 rows some statements came back with only the first page's rows (64% of rows at 400 rows, 2% at 1,600), and Amazon Bedrock rejected the 3,200-row requests as too long. Agentic extraction returned every row at every size with table parsing on, and 98% to 100% with it off. On these clean tables, table parsing also made agentic extraction cheaper: from 800 rows it cost less than single-pass even if every call billed at the long-context rate. Real invoices agree on agentic extraction, which found 67% of the line items against 17% for single-pass ([Agentic or single-pass extraction](#agentic-or-single-pass-extraction)), but not on table parsing, which didn't help on long real invoices ([Deterministic table parsing](#deterministic-table-parsing)). Test it on your own documents.
